comment: Client-side crypto / encrypt-decrypt logic locators (0.47.0). Scanned against JS bodies only (JsAnalyzer). Passive: these point an analyst at WHERE crypto happens for manual review; the 'note' says how to leverage it. Same {name,severity,regex,note} schema as secrets.json; all spans are explicitly bounded (ReDoS). Reported non-sensitive (evidence shown).

patterns.name: CryptoJS cipher usage
patterns.note: client-side crypto is reversible by the client -- find the key/IV/mode nearby and reproduce/decrypt offline (e.g. CyberChef); never a security control

patterns.name: Web Crypto API usage
patterns.note: trace where the key material comes from -- if it's shipped to the browser, you can reproduce the operation offline

patterns.name: forge crypto usage
patterns.note: check for a hardcoded key/private key nearby; client-side crypto can be reproduced offline

patterns.name: JSEncrypt client-side RSA
patterns.note: client-side RSA usually encrypts credentials before send -- the public key is in the JS; it stops passive sniffing only, not an authz/integrity control

patterns.name: SJCL crypto usage
patterns.note: look for the passphrase/key nearby; reproduce offline to decrypt

patterns.name: Weak cipher/hash algorithm
patterns.note: weak/broken primitive -- flag it; ECB leaks plaintext structure, MD5/SHA1/DES are collision/brute weak

patterns.name: Hardcoded crypto key/IV/salt
patterns.note: the key/IV is embedded in the client -- extract it and decrypt/forge whatever this code protects (e.g. CyberChef)

patterns.name: Base64 encode/decode (atob/btoa)
patterns.note: base64 is encoding, not encryption -- decode it to see what the app treats as 'hidden'

patterns.name: Client-side JWT signing
patterns.note: if the signing secret is in the JS you can forge arbitrary tokens -- extract it and mint a token with elevated claims
